t:
That—

        (a) The area bounded by Seventh Street, Independence Avenue, Ninth Street, and Jefferson Drive, in the District of Columbia, is hereby appropriated to the Smithsonian Institution as the permanent site of a museum and the area bounded by Seventh Street, Jefferson Drive, Ninth Street, and Madison Drive, in the District of Columbia is hereby made available to the Smithsonian Institution as the permanent site of a sculpture garden, both areas to be used for the exhibition of works of art. 
        (b) The Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution is authorized to remove any existing structure, to prepare architectural and engineering designs, plans, and specifications, and to construct a suitable museum within said area lying south of Jefferson Drive and to provide a sculpture garden for the use of the Smithsonian Institution within the areas designated in section 1(a) of this Act.

fable.w: The section only sets aside land in the District of Columbia for the Smithsonian and authorizes its Board of Regents to design and build a museum and sculpture garden. The tempting reading is that a "Board" signals an advisory body with outside members, but the Board of Regents is the Smithsonian's own governing body exercising its own authority, not outsiders being consulted on a federal decision. The section requires no comment period, hearing, consultation with states or the public, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution is authorized to remove any existing structure, to prepare architectural and engineering designs, plans, and specifications, and to construct a suitable museum

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution to construct a museum and sculpture garden. The Board of Regents is a federal entity (or at least an instrumentality of the federal government in this context), and the text describes internal administrative actions (construction, design) rather than consultation with outside parties. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees with outside members, or coordination with non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: The Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution is authorized to remove any existing structure, to prepare architectural and engineering designs, plans, and specifications, and to construct a suitable museum within said area lying south of Jefferson Drive and to provide a sculpture garden for the use of the Smithsonian Institution within the areas designated in section 1(a) of this Act.

opus.w: The section sets aside land for a Smithsonian museum and sculpture garden, and authorizes the Smithsonian's own Board of Regents to design and build them. The Board is the institution's governing body using its own authority, not an outside advisory body consulted before a federal decision. No hearing, comment period, outside consultation, or right to sue is provided, so the mention of a 'Board' does not make this participation.
opus.s: The Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution is authorized to remove any existing structure, to prepare architectural and engineering designs, plans, and specifications, and to construct a suitable museum
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is that the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution counts as outside participation, since several Regents are private citizens. That fails because the Board of Regents is the Smithsonian's own governing body. Here it acts as the decision-maker, carrying out its own authority to remove structures, design plans and build the museum. It is not an advisory body that a federal agency consults before deciding. The section has no comment period, hearing, consultation with states or outside entities, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Smithsonian Institution's Board of Regents to construct a museum and sculpture garden. The Smithsonian is a federal trust instrumentality, and its Board of Regents includes high-level federal officials (such as the Vice President and members of Congress), placing it inside the federal government boundary. There is no requirement to consult with outside parties, such as the public, states, or independent experts, before making the decision to build.
qwen_chat.s: The Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution is authorized to remove any existing structure, to prepare architectural and engineering designs, plans, and specifications, and to construct a suitable museum within said area lying south of Jefferson Drive and to provide a sculpture garden for the use of the Smithsonian Institution within the areas designated in section 1(a) of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Smithsonian Institution is an independent establishment and thus "outside" the federal government, so authorizing its Board of Regents to act constitutes participation. However, the Smithsonian is a federally funded trust instrumentality, and its Board of Regents includes the Vice President and members of Congress, making it effectively part of the federal government structure for the purposes of this definition. Furthermore, the section merely authorizes construction and design; it does not require consultation with the public, states, or other external entities before the decision to build is made.
